events.title: In the Room: Sixty Years on the Front Lines of History
events.description: Roosevelt understood the camera before most politicians did. He posed in buckskin in the Badlands, stood with John Muir at Yosemite, and left behind one of the most photographed lives of his century. David Hume Kennerly has spent sixty years doing the other half of that job — from the Vietnam battlefields that earned him the Pulitzer, to the Ford White House, to nearly every administration since. The special exhibition, drawn from his book In the Room, opens at the Library in October.

events.title: Lantern Tours at the Chateau de Mores
events.description: Step into history and mystery at the Chateau de Morès State Historic Site in Medora during the Chateau Lantern Tours. Explore the darker side of the Chateau’s past in a thrilling evening of frights, delights, and minimal lights. The one-hour tours are offered Oct. 23 and 24 at 6:30, 7, 7:30, 8, and 8:30 p.m.  After an introduction at the Interpretive Center, walk to the Chateau for a tour through the main level and upstairs. While venturing through the Chateau, illuminated by lanterns, hear tales of apparitions, ghost lights, murder, and more. Although nothing will jump out to frighten you, you never know what will be around the next corner. Tickets are $10 for adults and $5 for ages 6 to 17 and can be purchased in advance to ensure a reserved spot by calling 701.623.4355 or visiting the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center. Lanterns will be provided. Guests should dress warmly with the weather in mind. The Chateau de Morès is a historic home with narrow stairs, uneven floors, and other accessibility concerns. This event is part of the ND250 commemoration celebrating our country’s 250th birthday. For more information, contact Outreach Coordinator Shelby Reidle, shschateau@nd.gov or 701.623.4355. The Chateau de Morès State Historic Site is managed by the State Historical Society of North Dakota. The Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center and home are open daily from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. through Sept. 30. Beginning Oct. 1, the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center will be open Tuesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., and closed Sunday-Monday.

events.title: Explore Theodore Roosevelt National Park
events.description:
Come explore Theodore Roosevelt National Park! Come experience the national parks! On six days each year, all National Park Service sites that charge an entrance fee will offer free admission to everyone. Mark your calendar for these entrance fee–free dates:

February 16, 2026: Presidents Day (Washington’s Birthday) May 25, 2026: Memorial Day June 14, 2026: Flag Day July 3–5, 2026: Independence Day ( https://www.nps.gov/subjects/npscelebrates/july4th.htm ) weekend August 25, 2026: 110th Birthday of the National Park Service ( https://www.nps.gov/subjects/npscelebrates/nps-birthday.htm ) September 17, 2026: Constitution Day October 27, 2026: Theodore Roosevelt’s birthday November 11, 2026: Veterans Day ( https://www.nps.gov/subjects/npscelebrates/veterans-day.htm )

National parks are America’s best idea, and there are more than 400 parks ( https://www.nps.gov/findapark/index.htm ) available to everyone, every day. The fee-free days provide a great opportunity to visit a new place or an old favorite, especially one of the national parks that normally charge an entrance fee ( https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/fee-free-parks-state.htm ). The others are free all the time. The entrance fee waiver for fee-free days does not cover amenity or user fees for activities such as camping, boat launches, transportation, or special tours. The annual $80 America the Beautiful National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Pass allows unlimited entrance to more than 2,000 federal recreation areas, including all national parks that normally charge an entrance fee. There are also free or discounted passes available for senior citizens, current members of the military, families of fourth-grade students, and disabled citizens. Learn more about the variety of passes offered by the America the Beautiful National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands Pass ( https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/passes.htm ) series.

events.title: 13th Annual Trick or Trunk
events.description: 13th Annual Trick or Trunk Put on your favorite costume and join the Dickinson Area Chamber of Commerce for the 13th Annual Trick or Trunk on Saturday, October 31, from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM in Downtown Legacy Square and the two blocks surrounding City Hall. This free, family-friendly Halloween tradition brings together local businesses, organizations, and the community for an afternoon of trick-or-treating, festive fun, and plenty of candy! Children and families are invited to stroll through downtown, visit participating businesses and decorated trunks, and enjoy a safe and exciting Halloween experience. Event Highlights Trick-or-treating with local businesses and organizations Decorated trunks and festive displays Safe, family-friendly Halloween fun Thousands of pieces of candy for little ghosts and goblins Costumes encouraged for all ages! Best Decorated Trunk/Space Contest Returns! Participating businesses and organizations will once again compete for the title of Best Decorated Trunk/Space. Event attendees will have the opportunity to vote for their favorite display by scanning QR codes located throughout the event. Voting will close at the end of Trick or Trunk, and the winner will be announced on the Dickinson Area Chamber of Commerce's social media following the event. Whether you're a business looking to connect with the community or a family looking to celebrate Halloween, Trick or Trunk is an event you won't want to miss. Event Details Date: Saturday, October 31 Time: 3:00 PM – 5:00 PM Location: Downtown Legacy Square and the two blocks surrounding City Hall \(same route as last year\) Admission is free, so gather your family, wear your best costume, and join us for one of Dickinson's favorite Halloween traditions. We can't wait to celebrate with you!
